reviews.title: Great AI language learning tool!
reviews.text: I have been using Langua’s AI and flashcards for learning French in between tutoring sessions (also on Langua). My language skills and comfort in speaking are improving rapidly. It is easy to use  whenever I have a little time, and the conversations are so natural, really the next best thing to being in France and chatting with people. I highly recommend Langua!

reviews.title: Fantastic tool for speaking and learning
reviews.text: I am a B2 Spanish speaker eager to improve. Langua has been such a game changer! I talk to my tutor almost daily and have made great strides in a short time. Complicated grammar structures that I would have avoided in the past, I now use without having to think too much. What’s been really interesting is that because I am talking to an AI tutor, I can mention anything in the world, and they know something about it. We have discussed the Spanish Civil War, the concept of the Overton window, jazz vocalists, the writing styles of various authors, current events, etc. I am a huge fan!

reviews.title: Mandarin
reviews.text: It won’t let you preview vocabulary in pinyin. I like seeing tone marks on the words I want to learn. This app makes you read the characters which don’t have tone marks. The practice audio samples are all at different volumes so you may need to turn one way up to hear the tones then the next one will blast your ears. The live talking is often very laggy. Beware of the trial period. You can be locked into an expensive period with an app you don’t use.

reviews.title: Almost Perfect
reviews.text: This app is great for me as a high intermediate speaker. I love the natural style of conversations in call mode. I especially love the ability to highlight a word or phrase, get the definition, and save it automatically to my vocabulary pile— and then practice it in context. I have found the variety of topics and activities to be very satisfying, and I’ve been able to add a lot to my vocabulary as well. After using it for about a month, the app is targeted grammatical features I need to practice, too. The only two suggestions  I have would be to add more difficult dialects like Venezuelan and Dominican accents, and also to be able to highlight grammar notes and compile them in a notebook to review later.

reviews.title: Expectations not met
reviews.text:
After comparing AI apps for Spanish conversation using reviews, I chose Langua. I have been using it daily for a few weeks. I am disappointed with the AI conversations I have had. For one thing, the AI model seems at times not to understand my responses or questions. Sometimes, when I ask it how would you say such and such in English in Spanish it return with the English I asked the Spanish equivalent! 

I have not given up after spending $159 for a year subscription. But I am disappointed. An AI language app is only as good as its underlying AI model. Langua seems not to have a descent AI engine running the app.

reviews.title: Keeps getting better and better! So worth the subscription
reviews.text: I really love this app! It helps me squeeze in Spanish practice whenever I can throughout my day. I appreciate so much that the developers take feedback seriously and are continuously making improvements and enhancements for this app. I actually get excited to open it and look forward to the updates. I LOVE that I can make my own AI prompts! I’m really happy they included podcasts in the app too. I just hope that they can find a way to make it work with Apple Car Play so you can practice speaking while stuck in traffic.

reviews.title: Provides Extension to Basic Knowledge
reviews.text: Using Langua has helped to extend my second language practice into longer sentences and comprehension of more detailed natural speaking with the AI practice partners. My favorite part is reviewing the history & highlighting the phrases that are unknown; then generating to similar words or phrases to practice later with the flash cards. Also during discussions using the “light bulb” feature to generate sample answer choices and then record is efficient in getting a complete conversation in correct form to study and review. In my opinion, it’s better to study (read) a correct conversation (in writing) with grammar to build proficiency in speaking the language over time.

I like that I have options on how I want to be corrected. It’s very easy to highlight a specific word or phrase, get the translation, and add it to saved for later flash card work. Highly recommend!

reviews.title: Solid Product
reviews.text:
The heart of this app is the ai conversation interface. My priority is speaking fluency, natural conversation practice and targeted feedback. Langua was able to take me to the next level and exceeded my expectations.  I found the voices and accents extremely realistic and the feedback ecosystem outstanding.  The platform provides flexibility for every type of learning experience you may want to explore or review. 

This is a definite 5 star product and well worth the premium price. Additionally, they have indicated that they are committed to grow and improve this product for the future. 

The strengths of this app are conversation depth, quality of voices/accents, feedback quality, flexibility of learning. 

I feel the downsides are: 
While very flexible, it could add a layer of complexity in trying to identify the mode that provides the best results.
Higher price, but worth it.
The flash card section is not as robust as say a “Reverso”. (This would be my preference)
It may be a little difficult for an absolute beginner but the recent rollout of “My path” may solve this.

Background: 
I have been attempting to learn Italian for 3 years but freeze when I try to hold a conversation.  Also, I have trouble understanding Italian spoken by others. I have used apps like Duolingo and others, YouTube lessons, facebook communities, podcasts stories, Italian songs and videos, workbooks and several years of expensive lessons from online tutors. I also spent considerable time evaluating the whole range of ai learning products available prior to selecting Langua. 

Bottom line: Langua is a very cost effective way to take you to fluency and should be an important tool, but not the only one, in your language learning journey.  In just several weeks, it has helped me tremendously.

reviews.title: Numerous annoying flaws
reviews.text:
App doesn't properly start recording for several seconds after tapping start, causing the application to try to correct you on errors that weren't made. AI frequently forgets its own parameters during practice sessions, causing you to have to use your conversation credits to correct it. AI also frequently hallucinates that you are using an illogical homophone, and will "correct" perfectly sensible sentences. It seems like the AI is trained on people speaking a language poorly and fails more at unaccented comprehension than accented comprehension. If I put on a thick American accent, it understands me much better—how is that helpful  for practice?

EDIT: The appmaker said that this was a bug that they have corrected, which is an infuriating assertion given the fact it costs over $100 a year for a subscription and they aren't refunding users for the time it did not work. They also chose to contact me to boast about their large userbase as proof that their app works. Many people enjoying something doesn't make it inherently useful or good. Duolingo also has an enormous userbase, and has repeatedly been denounced for language acquisition. I would be skeptical of an app developer who thinks so little of your intelligence.

reviews.title: Yeah, Get It
reviews.text: I’m an introvert, so I avoid as much as possible talking with people. I’m also a bit of a cheapskate when it comes to learning languages because there are plenty of free options online. However, I gladly paid for a subscription to this program after my free trial was over. AI gives me the heebie jeebies, and I’m guilty of NIMBYism when it comes to data centers, but with the state of this country, I figured the benefits of being able to communicate with my fellow Americans outweighed my aversion to AI. This program is like having an amiable in-home tutor available 24/7. If you’re serious about learning a new language, I can’t recommend Langua enough. Well done, Developers!

reviews.title: Good, but tutors far too constrained.
reviews.text:
I use it for Spanish, about 90 minutes a day.

It is much better than other voice apps. Most recently I tried Practika and Duolingo, and it’s clearly more advanced. It’s good at hearing me and following my custom prompts. Like, sometimes I’ll just paste a whole song in Spanish, and it’s good at feeding me a line at a time to translate.

The main issue is the AI is incredibly reluctant to discuss a bunch of random things. Examples:

1. Anything related to sex. I didn’t expect it to write erotica, but it has trouble even mentioning the word for a private part. Like I mentioned trying to have a baby, not in a sexual way; it asked what a goal in my life right now is. I said “trying to have a baby. My wife and I have been trying for a while.” And it started into “I want to keep this conversation respectful, so let’s change the topic.”

I guess we got too close to the act of “trying to make a baby”.

2. Anything not real. This is the really weird one. Like I asked a silly question about “if you had to pick one of your fingers, and all your other fingers would become an exact copy of that finger, which would you pick?” And it just REFUSED to answer. It said something like “I want to keep this conversation respectful. There is no known method to change your fingers to be copies of the other.” I tried a few more times to get it to give a real response, and it just refused. 

3. Any ethical problem. I tried getting it to answer the trolley problem, and it mostly refused to answer. It kept refusing outright, or saying it would “find a way to save everyone”. Eventually, I did get it to say it would change the track to save 5/kill 1, but it was like pulling teeth.

In general, I find most conversations in real life can veer into made up-scenarios, or thought experiments, and the AI just cannot do those. Anything slightly unrealistic and it’ll refuse. 

It also can’t talk in anyway that isn’t overly professional. I really wanted to practice talking with actual Spanish speakers, the vast majority of whom are not super professional, super polite all the time, but it just can’t. I write a 2000 word prompt telling it to take in a ‘mean character’ and giving a ton of details of how it should talk to be more mean/sarcastic/etc., but it just refused and went yo it’s usual “overly nice” persona.
